title: What is known about 1RB0RC_1RC1RA_1LD0RA_0LE1RA_---1LF_1RB0LF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RC_1RC1RA_1LD0RA_0LE1RA_---1LF_1RB0LF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The head sweeps between the ends and each sweep adds about one cell at an end, so time is about quadratic in the width. Lean proves the shift rules and that C meeting 1^(2n+2) 0 halts at once; the run has never met it in 1010 steps, but the right end is not decoded.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: Halting family
claims.text: C going right over 1^(2n+2) 0 halts within 2n + 5 steps, for every n and every tape around: it erases the ones (C1 = 0RA, A1 = 0RC), writes a 1 on the 0 and turns into D going left, D reads the 0 just written and turns into E, and E reads another 0.

claims.title: Shift rules, for every length
claims.text: C going right turns (11)^n into (00)^n, and so does A.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 70,681 cells have been visited and 35,120 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.504). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.077).

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: tools/c/tmrun.c: 1010 steps from blank tape without a halt (176,203 ones). In the first 109 steps D reads a 0 (and turns into E) 6,959,030 times, and E always reads a 1.

claims.title: No closed tape language from windows up to 7
claims.text: bbtools.ctl with K = 2 to 7 closes but allows a halt (10 to 450 abstract halting configurations, E reading 0 inside the tape).

claims.title: Three parts of the tape
claims.text: At the steps where F reaches a new cell on the left: the left end runs through a cycle of about ten prefixes (one new cell each), the middle is (1 0 1 0^8)^k with k growing by about one per cycle (16 blocks at step 19,164, 104 at 356,532, 497 at 6,664,000), and the right end, written with a = 10 and b = 110, is a string such as 0a000abbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbba0aa000abbbbbbbba00000aa000ab… whose runs of b grow and collapse with no pattern decoded. Width 5,692 at step 6,664,000: about 0.2·w2 steps.

claims.title: Does it halt?
claims.text: Not known. What is left is the right end: whether a sweep ever brings C onto an even run of 1s followed by a 0 (or another E-on-0 pattern).

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1RD_1LC0RD_0LE1RD_1RA0RB_---1LF_1RA0LF up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 70,681 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: A cycling left end, a periodic middle, an irregular right end
html: F sweeps left erasing 1s (F1 = 0LF) and turns right at a 0; A, B and C sweep right. Each time F reaches a new cell on the left, the tape is a short prefix from a cycle of about ten, a middle of identical blocks and a right end:
(right end with a = 10, b = 110). The middle gains about one block per cycle of the left end; the tape width grows linearly with the number of sweeps, so the time is about quadratic in the width.

sections.heading: C on an even run of 1s
html: The only halt is E reading a 0, and E comes only from D reading a 0. Lean proves that C going right over an even, nonzero run of 1s followed by a 0 halts at once: C and A erase the ones in turn, C writes a 1 on the 0 and turns left as D, which finds the last erased cell and turns into E, which finds the one before. In the run, D found a 0 about 7 million times in 109 steps, and E always read a 1 after it.
Whether the irregular right end ever sets up that pattern is the open question.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.504). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.077).
After 109 steps the tape spans 70,681 cells (51,623 left of the start, 129 right), with a density of 1s of 0.497.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A bouncer whose tape is three parts: a left end that cycles through about ten prefixes, a middle of identical blocks 1010^8 that gains one block per cycle, and a right end of runs of 110 and 10 that changes irregularly; the machine halts as soon as C crosses an even run of 1s followed by a 0, which Lean proves.
family: Bouncer with a periodic middle and an irregular right end
